catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class expresses a fixed-request, input-free ROS service whose only output is an empty acknowledgement. cap.motion.stop.v1 declares a deceleration input and stopped/stopping-position outputs, but the pinned Stop.srv takes only Empty input and returns Empty output; using that class would invent a deceleration parameter and a stopped measurement the callback does not report.

No catalogue class expresses an input-free acknowledged emergency-stop service with no deceleration or stopped-state output. cap.motion.stop.v1 is a motion-stop class with a deceleration profile and stopped/stopping-position outputs, none of which the pinned ApplyEmergencyStop.srv accepts or reports. The callback is acknowledgement only and the driver does not claim a physical emergency stop.

notes:
Passed the fake gate on the pinned clone; the evidence state is contract_checked, not an MHS-Device level. This is a configuration-only RosDriver for the C++ kortex_driver node; no Python native class is declared. Scope is exactly the acknowledged ROS 1 services base/stop and base/apply_emergency_stop. Nothing else is bound: no joint or Cartesian motion, no gripper commands, no base/clear_faults or other reset/reenable service, no base/stop_sequence, base/stop_action or base/stop_teaching, no state, joint, controller or notification topic, and no node shutdown. The two service callbacks only call the Kortex API and return a boolean; a true callback is acknowledgement that the API call did not raise, not sensed zero velocity, a stopping position, a physical emergency stop or power isolation. The driver does not expose any state observation from which one could infer those. The relative upstream registrations base/stop and base/apply_emergency_stop are recorded as source_name; the configured /my_gen3 prefix is an explicit deployment assumption and operator configuration, so the operator must launch the node in that namespace or remap both services to the declared absolute endpoints. The request is the pinned nested Empty shape {'input': {}} and the response predicate requires {'output': {}} with rosbridge service_response.result true; the output acknowledged=true is written only after both checks. The package-local fake subclasses RecordingRosTransport and models only those two endpoints and response shapes. Tests cover service_response.result=false, a missing output, a wrong output and a failed emergency-stop reply; all stay failures. No fabricated stopped flag or state is returned. The fake is F0 contract evidence with no ROS node, Kortex API, controller dynamics or hardware; its failure switches and call record are placeholders, and no fidelity declaration is added to this hardware class. R2 is set from the robot arm, above the card's R0 floor. The input-free apply_emergency_stop Action is safe_state=True and the same fixed-request service is the safety_bindings.estop native stop. No estop_physical_ref is set because the clone contains no independent physical stop text and the callback acknowledgement is not one. driver.lock.json keeps reviewed_by null; the SDK refuses every ROS hardware backend without a human hardware review, and no hardware, ROS graph or rosbridge connection was used. The clone remains unmodified and no install command was run. No numeric inputs exist, so no Limit is declared; expected G8 warning G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE: SAFE-014 has nothing to probe and the suite awards CL2, while every other CL3 test passed. The gate reported no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning. NOT COVERED: the upstream node's simulation services and simulator, motion, gripper, fault clearing, other stop variants, all state observations, ROS launch/remapping, live ROS compatibility and hardware behavior. The fake records two apply_emergency_stop calls per e-stop when the runtime runs the native binding and then the safe-state action; both are acknowledgements and neither is a physical-stop claim.
